logs.summary:
Greece faced severe wildfires in late July and early August 2026, with a major blaze northwest of Athens destroying over 100 homes and burning thousands of hectares. On August 2, two firefighting helicopters collided in mid-air near Psatha, killing two crew members. By August 3, water-dropping aircraft continued to battle the fires, which had been fueled by extreme winds and record-breaking heat, with over 200 fires reported across the country since July 27.
On August 3, the wildfire west of Athens flared up again, requiring continued water-bombing aircraft operations. By August 4, firefighters seized a break in high winds to reinforce containment lines, while some residents returned to damaged homes, though forecasters warned that stronger gusts and rising temperatures were expected to return. The blaze, part of over 200 fires across Greece since late July, remained a threat amid a record-breaking heatwave and drought.

More than 100 homes were destroyed overnight this weekend in blazes that broke out around the coastal village of Porto Germeno. Hundreds of people have been evacuated. This is a local resident. Giorgos Mavroidis: “It’s not a good situation. This is extremely sad. The wind is very strong and keeps changing direction. It’s difficult to deal with. The firefighters, who are trained and experienced, can’t contain it. How can we?” Meanwhile, Hungary has temporarily shut down the country’s sole nuclear power plant for the first time in more than four decades amid a scorching heat wave and severe drought that triggered water-use restrictions in more than 100 cities and villages. In more related news, Britain’s National Farmers’ Union warns rising heat and a water drought could lead to shortages of certain foods in parts of England. This is at least the third drought in five years, with some areas of England not seeing rain in over a month. Here in the United States, in Washington state, nearly 65,000 people have received evacuation orders amid intensifying wildfires around the city of Spokane. Local officials say blazes in the region have destroyed more than 700 homes and businesses.

news.headline: Europe's hot, dry summer takes its toll with fires in France and Greece, and drought in the UK
news.body: Europe is grappling with a record-breaking hot and dry summer. Water-dropping planes on Monday tackled a major wildfire in Greece while firefighters in France worked to stabilize a blaze in Provence. The United Kingdom recorded its driest July in nearly two centuries. Strong winds returned in Greece, pushing flames into mountain home clusters, destroying farms and property, and closing a highway. In France, firefighters guarded against flare-ups near Bordeaux. The U.K. weather service reported a prolonged heat wave and lack of rainfall. Europe is the fastest-warming continent, with rising temperatures and droughts making wildfires more intense.
